## Setup & parameters

Adjust `data_dir` to point to wherever the GeoPackage files live.
Adjust `N` and the noise bounds to explore different parameter choices.

```{r}
#| label: setup

set.seed(123)  # global seed for full reproducibility

library(sf)
library(sfnetworks)
library(tidygraph)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tmap)

# --- paths ---
data_dir  <- "data"
out_dir   <- "public/Paths-and-Flows-3"
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Monte Carlo parameters ---
N          <- 500    # iterations (200 is fine for the exercise; 500 gives smoother results)
noise_min  <- 0.8   # lower edge-weight multiplier (-20%)
noise_max  <- 1.2   # upper edge-weight multiplier (+20%)
```

---

## Part 1: Monte Carlo Pi

### Estimate

```{r}
#| label: pi-estimate

N_pi  <- 10000
x     <- runif(N_pi, -1, 1)
y     <- runif(N_pi, -1, 1)
inside <- x^2 + y^2 <= 1
pi_hat <- 4 * sum(inside) / N_pi

cat("π estimate:", round(pi_hat, 5), "\n")
cat("True π:    ", round(pi,     5), "\n")
cat("Error:     ", round(abs(pi_hat - pi), 5), "\n")
```

### Plot — points inside / outside

```{r}
#| label: pi-plot

data.frame(x, y, inside = factor(inside, labels = c("Outside", "Inside"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = inside)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.4) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Outside" = "gray70", "Inside" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Monte Carlo Pi · N = ", N_pi),
    subtitle = paste0("π ≈ ", round(pi_hat, 4)),
    color    = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Convergence with N

Error decreases proportional to $1/\sqrt{N}$ — doubling accuracy requires 4× the samples.

```{r}
#| label: pi-convergence

N_conv <- 100000
xc <- runif(N_conv, -1, 1)
yc <- runif(N_conv, -1, 1)
pi_running <- cumsum(xc^2 + yc^2 <= 1) / seq_along(xc) * 4

data.frame(n = 1:N_conv, pi_hat = pi_running) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, pi_hat)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pi, color = "tomato", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = pi + 0.05, label = "true π",
           color = "tomato", hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "Convergence of Monte Carlo π estimate",
    x        = "N (log scale)",
    y        = "Estimated π"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Part 2: Network Monte Carlo

### Load data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

streets      <- read_sf(file.path(data_dir, "netzwerkanalyse.gpkg"),
                        layer = "osm_highway_prepared")
municipality <- read_sf(file.path(data_dir, "netzwerkanalyse.gpkg"),
                        layer = "Gemeinde_Waedenswil")
locations    <- read_sf(file.path(data_dir, "routing_locations.gpkg"))

net <- as_sfnetwork(streets, directed = FALSE) |>
  activate("edges") |>
  mutate(length = edge_length())

edges <- st_as_sf(net, "edges")
nodes <- st_as_sf(net, "nodes")

cat("Nodes:    ", nrow(nodes), "\n")
cat("Edges:    ", nrow(edges), "\n")
cat("Locations:", nrow(locations), "—",
    paste(sort(locations$name), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

### Baseline route

```{r}
#| label: baseline

spitzen <- locations |> filter(name == "Spitzen")
bahnhof <- locations |> filter(name == "Bahnhof")

baseline <- st_network_paths(net,
  from    = spitzen,
  to      = bahnhof,
  weights = "length")

baseline_idx   <- baseline |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist()
baseline_edges <- net |>
  activate("edges") |>
  slice(baseline_idx) |>
  st_as_sf()

cat("Baseline route:", nrow(baseline_edges), "segments,",
    round(sum(as.numeric(baseline_edges$length))), "m\n")

p_baseline <- tm_shape(edges) +
  tm_lines(col = "gray85") +
  tm_shape(baseline_edges, is.main = TRUE) +
  tm_lines(col = "steelblue", lwd = 2) +
  tm_shape(bind_rows(spitzen, bahnhof)) +
  tm_dots() +
  tm_text("name", ymod = 0.5) +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Baseline shortest path: Spitzen → Bahnhof",
            inner.margins = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1))

tmap_save(p_baseline, file.path(out_dir, "task1-baseline.png"), width = 30, height = 20,units = "cm")
p_baseline
```

### Single perturbation (sanity check)

Run once with a fixed seed so the result is reproducible here.
Overlay the perturbed route on the baseline — if they never differ, noise is too small.

```{r}
#| label: single-perturbation

set.seed(42)

net_noisy <- net |>
  activate("edges") |>
  mutate(length_noisy = as.numeric(length) *
           runif(n(), min = noise_min, max = noise_max))

noisy_path  <- st_network_paths(net_noisy,
  from    = spitzen,
  to      = bahnhof,
  weights = "length_noisy")

noisy_edges <- net_noisy |>
  activate("edges") |>
  slice(noisy_path |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist()) |>
  st_as_sf()

# How many segments differ?
n_differ <- length(setdiff(
  baseline |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist(),
  noisy_path |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist()
))
cat("Segments in baseline but not noisy path:", n_differ, "\n")

p_perturb <- tm_shape(edges) +
  tm_lines(col = "gray85") +
  tm_shape(baseline_edges, is.main = TRUE) +
  tm_lines(col = "steelblue", lwd = 2) +
  tm_shape(noisy_edges) +
  tm_lines(col = "tomato", lwd = 1.5) +
  tm_shape(bind_rows(spitzen, bahnhof)) +
  tm_dots() +
  tm_text("name", ymod = 0.5) +
  tm_layout(
    main.title = paste0("Baseline (blue) vs. one perturbed route (red)"),
  )

tmap_save(p_perturb, file.path(out_dir, "task2-perturbation.png"), width = 30, height = 20,units = "cm")
p_perturb
```

### Monte Carlo loop

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo
#| cache: true

set.seed(123)

edge_count    <- rep(0L, nrow(edges))
route_true_m  <- numeric(N)   # true (unperturbed) length of each chosen route

for (i in seq_len(N)) {
  # 1. perturb
  net_i <- net |>
    activate("edges") |>
    mutate(
      length_noisy = as.numeric(length) *
        runif(n(), min = noise_min, max = noise_max)
    )

  # 2. shortest path under perturbed weights
  path_i <- st_network_paths(net_i,
    from    = spitzen,
    to      = bahnhof,
    weights = "length_noisy")

  idx <- path_i |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist()

  # 3. accumulate
  edge_count[idx] <- edge_count[idx] + 1L

  # 4. record the TRUE length of the chosen route (not the perturbed weight)
  route_true_m[i] <- net |>
    activate("edges") |>
    slice(idx) |>
    st_as_sf() |>
    pull(length) |>
    as.numeric() |>
    sum()
}

edges <- edges |> mutate(freq = edge_count / N)

cat("Monte Carlo loop complete.\n")
```

### Frequency map

```{r}
#| label: freq-map

p_freq <- tm_shape(edges |> filter(freq == 0)) +
  tm_lines(col = "gray90") +
  tm_shape(edges |> filter(freq > 0), is.main = TRUE) +
  tm_lines(col = "freq", palette = "inferno", style = "cont",
           breaks = c(0, 1), title.col = "Route\nfrequency") +
  tm_shape(bind_rows(spitzen, bahnhof)) +
  tm_dots() +
  tm_text("name", ymod = 0.5) +
  tm_layout(
    main.title = paste0("Route uncertainty: Spitzen → Bahnhof"),
  )

tmap_save(p_freq, file.path(out_dir, "task4-frequency.png"), width = 30, height = 20,units = "cm")
p_freq
```

### Diagnostics

Does the result look interesting? We want:

- A non-trivial robust core (some segments always appear)
- Some contested segments (intermediate freq) — if there are none, the noise is too small
- Not everything contested (if most freq < 0.5, noise may be too large)

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics

active <- edges |> filter(freq > 0)

cat("=== Edge frequency summary ===\n")
cat("Total edges in network:        ", nrow(edges), "\n")
cat("Edges that appeared (freq > 0):", nrow(active), "\n")
cat("Robust core    (freq > 0.9):   ", sum(edges$freq > 0.9), "\n")
cat("Contested      (0.1–0.9 freq): ", sum(edges$freq > 0.1 & edges$freq < 0.9), "\n")
cat("Rare           (0 < freq ≤ 0.1):", sum(edges$freq > 0 & edges$freq <= 0.1), "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("=== Route length (true, unperturbed) ===\n")
cat("Deterministic baseline:  ", round(sum(as.numeric(baseline_edges$length))), "m\n")
cat("Mean of MC routes:       ", round(mean(route_true_m)), "m\n")
cat("SD of MC routes:         ", round(sd(route_true_m)), "m\n")
cat("Range:                   ", round(min(route_true_m)), "–",
    round(max(route_true_m)), "m\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: freq-histogram

ggplot(data.frame(freq = edges$freq[edges$freq > 0]), aes(x = freq)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.1, 0.9), linetype = "dashed", color = "tomato") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.05, y = Inf, label = "rare", vjust = 2,
           color = "tomato", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = Inf, label = "contested", vjust = 2,
           color = "tomato", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.95, y = Inf, label = "robust", vjust = 2,
           color = "tomato", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of edge frequencies (edges with freq > 0 only)",
    x        = "Frequency in optimal path",
    y        = "Number of edges"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: route-length-dist

ggplot(data.frame(length_m = route_true_m), aes(x = length_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sum(as.numeric(baseline_edges$length)),
             color = "tomato", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = sum(as.numeric(baseline_edges$length)),
           y = Inf, label = " deterministic\n baseline",
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, color = "tomato", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of route lengths across MC iterations",
    subtitle = "True (unperturbed) length of whichever route was chosen",
    x        = "Route length (m)",
    y        = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Sensitivity analysis — three noise levels

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
#| cache: true

run_mc <- function(net, from, to, N, noise_min, noise_max) {
  n_edges    <- nrow(st_as_sf(net, "edges"))
  edge_count <- rep(0L, n_edges)

  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    net_i <- net |>
      activate("edges") |>
      mutate(length_noisy = as.numeric(length) *
               runif(n(), min = noise_min, max = noise_max))

    path_i <- st_network_paths(net_i, from, to,
                                weights = "length_noisy")
    if (nrow(path_i) == 0) next

    idx <- path_i |> pull(edge_paths) |> unlist()
    edge_count[idx] <- edge_count[idx] + 1L
  }
  edge_count / N
}

set.seed(123)
freq_low  <- run_mc(net, spitzen, bahnhof, N, 0.9, 1.1)   # ±10%
freq_mid  <- run_mc(net, spitzen, bahnhof, N, 0.8, 1.2)   # ±20%
freq_high <- run_mc(net, spitzen, bahnhof, N, 0.5, 1.5)   # ±50%
```

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-table

data.frame(
  noise     = c("±10%", "±20%", "±50%"),
  robust    = c(sum(freq_low  > 0.9),
                sum(freq_mid  > 0.9),
                sum(freq_high > 0.9)),
  contested = c(sum(freq_low  > 0.1 & freq_low  < 0.9),
                sum(freq_mid  > 0.1 & freq_mid  < 0.9),
                sum(freq_high > 0.1 & freq_high < 0.9)),
  rare      = c(sum(freq_low  > 0  & freq_low  <= 0.1),
                sum(freq_mid  > 0  & freq_mid  <= 0.1),
                sum(freq_high > 0  & freq_high <= 0.1))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-maps
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

edges_sens <- bind_rows(
  edges |> mutate(freq = freq_low,  noise = "±10%"),
  edges |> mutate(freq = freq_mid,  noise = "±20%"),
  edges |> mutate(freq = freq_high, noise = "±50%")
) |>
  mutate(noise = factor(noise, levels = c("±10%", "±20%", "±50%")))

tm_shape(edges_sens |> filter(freq == 0)) +
  tm_lines(col = "gray90") +
  tm_shape(edges_sens |> filter(freq > 0), is.main = TRUE) +
  tm_lines(col = "freq", palette = "inferno", style = "cont",
           breaks = c(0, 1), title.col = "Route\nfrequency") +
  tm_facets(by = "noise", ncol = 3) +
  tm_layout(main.title = paste0("Route uncertainty at three noise levels · N = ", N, " iterations"))
```

### Interpretation guide

Use the sensitivity table and maps to decide whether the exercise parameters need adjustment:

| What you see | Diagnosis | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Most edges have `freq ≈ 1` even at ±20% | Noise too small, no interesting variation | Increase to ±50% |
| `freq` is uniform ~0.1–0.3, no clear core | Noise too large, route is essentially random | Reduce to ±10% |
| Clear bright core + some purple alternatives | **Sweet spot — interesting result** | Use these parameters |
| Very few contested edges (< 5) | Route has no good alternatives; still pedagogically valid | Fine as-is, explain network structure |
